bullets.title: US-Iran MOU: Hormuz to reopen within 30 days; oil plunges 4-5%
bullets.body: A US-Iran memorandum of understanding stipulates reopening the Strait of Hormuz within 30 days, with US forces withdrawing from surrounding Iran. Despite the headline, Iran's IRNA clarified it makes no commitment on Strait management (future governance resolved regionally with Oman), and no nuclear agreement was reached—talks resume within 60 days. Brent fell 4-5% on the news while markets spiked; JPMorgan's base case remains a narrow deal extending a fragile truce without resolving nuclear/missile/proxy issues, and flags accidental escalation risk remains elevated.

bullets.title: Broader market rallies: S&P +0.7% to 7,443; Mag7 all green premarket
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures extended gains 0.7% (7,443 level), Nasdaq +0.6%, with the entire Mag7 higher in premarket—Alphabet +1.3%, Meta/Amazon +1%, Tesla +0.7%, Nvidia/Microsoft +0.6%, Apple +0.4%. VIX rose 4.4% to 18.58. Hedgeye notes SPX dealer gamma flips positive; VIX breakdown below 18.87 would be additionally bullish with all-time highs (7,619 risk range top) still in play.

bullets.title: Fed FOMC preview: No 2026 cuts, easing bias stripped, PCE revised higher
bullets.body: Consensus across multiple desks: Fed holds at 3.50-3.75% next week, removes easing bias, and revises up both headline and core PCE projections (one desk sees core PCE rising from 2.7% to 3.2%). Median dot plot expected to show no 2026 cuts and 50bp reduction only by 2028, with 2-3 participants projecting 50-75bp of tightening this year. Chair Warsh expected to acknowledge inflation persistence while speaking optimistically about AI-driven productivity. JPMorgan raised YE26 2-year forecast to 4.20% (from 3.90%) and 10-year to 4.70% (from 4.50%).

bullets.title: ECB hiked 25bp to 2.25%; staff projections imply up to four total hikes
bullets.body: ECB delivered a unanimous 25bp hike; staff projections are consistent with four total hikes, though JPMorgan forecasts only two (one more in September). Core inflation projections raised +0.2-0.3pt to 2.5% in both 2026 and 2027. ECB assumes oil declines from $97/bbl in 2026 to $82 in 2027; even in a mild Iran deal scenario, staff sees core inflation above 2% in 2028 and three hikes likely. ECB's Rehn reiterated no pre-commitment to any particular rate path.

bullets.title: Geopolitical oil risk: $100/bbl base case persists; adverse scenario is $150
bullets.body: JPMorgan forecasts Hormuz reopening likely by mid-2026 but oil lingers near $100/bbl due to demand absorption; global GDP growth revised down 0.3pt to 2.3% for 2026, global CPI inflation revised up 1pt to 3.6%. An adverse scenario with oil at $150/bbl would be a larger shock than 2022. Global oil supply is ~13 mbd short, met by ~6 mbd inventory draws and ~6 mbd demand destruction. Germany's Economy Ministry said no strategic crude reserve releases are needed.

bullets.title: SpaceX IPO trades today at $135; gray-market and derivatives signal 30-50% pop
bullets.body: SpaceX (SPCX) listed on Nasdaq with quotation at 9:50am ET and trading at 10am ET. Gray-market and derivatives pricing imply a 30-50% first-day jump (market cap ~$2.2-2.4T for 20-30% gain); probability models show 62% odds of 20%+ gain (up from 20% prior day). Wolfe initiated with Outperform and $175 PT (29.6% upside from $135 IPO price), with Starship reusability as the critical value unlock that could expand gross margins 10pts to 80%+ and reduce launch cost from $14M to ~$4M per 100t payload. Starlink already recouped its $10B investment and is projected to reach $90B EBITDA/year by 2030.

bullets.title: SpaceX IPO supply wave + AI IPO pipeline cited as headwind for existing AI equities
bullets.body: Multiple desks flag that the SpaceX IPO and potential upcoming OpenAI/Anthropic IPOs worth hundreds of billions represent a supply wave that pulled back AI equities. UBS notes AI Winners index +5.75% and SOX +7.9% day-over-day, but software/IGV -0.72% with equity L/S funds de-grossing US equities and selling crowded Mag7 names. Tech adjusted for Amazon, Google, and Meta now exceeds 51% of S&P 500.

bullets.title: Token price deflation hits AI infrastructure trade; energy/power names recovering
bullets.body: Silicon Data LLM Token Expenditure Index shows dropping token pricing—a near-term headwind for the AI infrastructure buildout trade as investors reconsider ROI. High Performance Compute, Power Semis, and Nuclear are most sensitive given frontier model revenue impact on infrastructure urgency. Energy/power-adjacent baskets (nuclear, bitcoin miners, power semis, AI power) posted largest one-day recoveries, carrying heavy embedded inflation risk premium. Banks also raised financing costs for leveraged bets on popular AI plays.

bullets.title: Consumer sentiment weak but actual spending resilient; softlines prices +3% y/y
bullets.body: U Mich headline sentiment rose 4.1pts to 48.9 in early June on gas relief but remains below prior recession and Covid lows; 38% of respondents cite inflation as top risk (high since Feb 2025) and 47% expect rate increases. PSC's daily survey (500 respondents/night vs U Mich's 1k/month) tracks spending far more closely and is bottoming well above prior lows—real consumer spending was up 2.1% y/y in April. UBS Evidence Lab shows softgoods out-the-door prices up 3% y/y in May (+7% on 2-year basis), suggesting companies are successfully offsetting tariff costs.

bullets.title: Nasdaq-100 rebalancing: NBIS, CRWV, ALAB added; CHTR removed
bullets.body: The Nasdaq-100 is adding Nebius (NBIS), CoreWeave (CRWV), and Astera Labs (ALAB), while removing Charter Communications (CHTR). All three additions are AI/data center infrastructure names and are rallying premarket on the passive rebalancing demand.

bullets.title: Non-AI cyclicals setup improving as growth/inflation expectations decline orderly
bullets.body: 22V and multiple desks argue an orderly slowdown from 2.7% to ~2% GDP growth with declining inflation is a positive setup for non-AI cyclicals (retail, regional banks, airlines, homebuilders) if 10-year yields stay in the 4.2-4.5% range. Retail stocks experienced PE compression despite +17% EPS estimate increases; financials sector positioning at only the 17th percentile per Deutsche Bank. BofA Bull & Bear Indicator is at 8.8 (sell signal territory) but historically only precedes 2-3% pullbacks in the near term.

bullets.title: OBBBA tax provisions could lift S&P 500 FCF by 1%+; hyperscalers key winners
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes the One Big Beautiful Budget Act restores bonus depreciation, enables immediate R&D expensing, and adds FDDEI provisions—collectively could lift S&P 500 FCF by 1%+. Hyperscalers are the primary beneficiaries given large R&D deductions and bonus depreciation on incremental AI capex; tariff revenue offsets also ease Treasury financing pressures.

bullets.title: U.S. equity supply flipped positive for first time since 2021; tech saw record weekly inflows
bullets.body: Tech had the biggest weekly inflow ever at $12.3B with semiconductor ETFs capturing $5.9B. Separately, SOXL alone generated ~$12B in net rebalancing demand equal to ~45% of prior-day AUM, highlighting leveraged ETFs' growing role in market structure. U.S. equity supply has turned positive to +$124B annualized for the first time since 2021, historically a headwind for equities. Market has shifted to negative gamma regime with ~$5B per 1% move from options and ~$8B from leveraged ETFs amplifying volatility.

bullets.title: China semiconductor supply chain risk: WF6 and tungsten embargoes disrupting Japan
bullets.body: China's export controls on tungsten brought Japan's semiconductor gas production to zero, threatening TSMC, SK Hynix, and Samsung supply chains. Separately, China's WF6 export controls disrupted Japan's semiconductor supply chain in what analysts characterize as part of broader AI supremacy supply chain weaponization. China credit data was strong—May aggregate financing 17.48T CNY (est. 17.15T) and M1 growth beat at 5.5% vs 5.0% expected.

bullets.title: KOSPI +4.6% overnight; Citi raises target to 10,000 on semiconductor upcycle
bullets.body: KOSPI held Hedgeye's trade signal support and rallied 4.6% overnight. Citi raised its KOSPI target to 10,000 (from 8,500) based on 2.3x BVPS, with FY26E net profit forecast to improve +231% YoY on semiconductor-driven GDP growth. Memory supply shortages projected to persist with upcycle extending into 2027; top picks focus on AI chip demand, US-Korea manufacturing cooperation (shipbuilding, power, nuclear), and wealth effect plays. SK Hynix is also reportedly planning a US Nasdaq listing by August to capitalize on the AI boom.

bullets.title: Online ad spend accelerating to +16% in 2026; Cannes AI monetization is key theme
bullets.body: Citi projects US online ad spend to accelerate to +16% Y/Y in 2026E from +13% in 2025A, with digital ad penetration at ~80%. Google's AI Mode queries run ~3x longer than traditional queries creating richer intent signals; Google launched five new AI Search ad formats. OpenAI's Ads Manager Beta is live across 9 countries via Criteo partnership. Citi's top picks heading into Cannes: GOOGL, AMZN, META, RDDT, APP.

bullets.title: Inference-driven front-end networking refresh lifts ANET and CSCO price targets
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised ANET PT to $190 and CSCO PT to $130, arguing AI agents produce 450% more traffic than humans and the move to 1:1 CPU-to-GPU ratios expands front-end network demand sharply. Dell'Oro estimates AI front-end networking spend grows from $1.8B (2025) to $6.3B by 2030 at 29% CAGR with upside case to $10B. ANET targets $3.5B in AI revenue, CSCO targets $4B in FY26.

bullets.title: Data center permitting/local opposition emerging as new constraint alongside power
bullets.body: Charlotte joins North Carolina jurisdictions imposing 150-day data center construction moratoriums; permitting and local opposition are emerging as a development constraint alongside power and labor. Anthropic is pursuing its first direct data center leases (>1GW letter of intent), moving from cloud rental to tenant model. Applied Digital signed a 210MW lease at Delta Forge 2 worth ~$5.2B base-term. Amazon's Leo satellite constellation received a conditional waiver rather than extension and must deploy 3,232 satellites by July 2029.

bullets.title: Macro setup framed as 'Peace Quad 1': bonds, oil, stocks converging on Iran resolution
bullets.body: Multiple macro sources (Hedgeye, 22V, SPY technicals) frame the current setup as a bullish Quad 1 backdrop—slower growth, declining inflation, falling oil, and geopolitical de-escalation all pointing in the same direction. One analyst notes stocks, bonds, oil, and prediction markets are all converging on near-certainty that Iran conflict is over, but warns the risk is escalation takes longer or becomes messier than priced. Copper is +2.3% as one of the few remaining commodity longs.

bullets.title: US IBs outperforming EU peers; GS/MS best-positioned on ECM and equities gearing
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised 2026E adj. EPS ~2% across Global IBs on stronger equities revenues (+13% YoY vs +7% prior). US IBs positioned to outperform EU peers on earnings momentum, balance sheet growth, and IPO financing tailwinds. GS and MS flagged as best positioned on maximum equities gearing (ECM + Equities S&T); GS moves to positive catalyst watch ahead of July 14 Q2 results. Oil volatility +129% YoY providing additional US advantage in commodities.
